CPDV.text: The Lord will provide retribution on my behalf. O Lord, your mercy is forever. Do not disdain the works of your hands.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord will provide retribution on my behalf. O Lord, your mercy is forever. Do not disdain the works of your hands.

verses.context: Trusting that God will finish what concerns him despite present trouble, David asks God not to abandon the work of his own hands.

KJV.text: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
KJV.displayText: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.

BSB.text: The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth.

CPDV.text: The Lord is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth.

verses.context: Still praising God's character in this acrostic psalm, David notes that the Lord stays near to everyone who calls on him sincerely.

KJV.text: Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God:
KJV.displayText: Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God:

BSB.text: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
BSB.displayText: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,

CPDV.text: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob: his hope is in the Lord God himself,
CPDV.displayText: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob: his hope is in the Lord God himself,

verses.context: After warning against trusting powerful people who eventually die, this psalm calls truly happy the one whose hope rests instead in the God of Jacob.

KJV.text: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.
KJV.displayText: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

BSB.text: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion.

CPDV.text: The Lord is well pleased with those who fear him and with those who hope in his mercy.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is well pleased with those who fear him and with those who hope in his mercy.

verses.context: This psalm of praise notes that what pleases the Lord is not raw strength, like a fast horse, but people who fear him and hope in his mercy.

KJV.text: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
KJV.displayText: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

BSB.text: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
BSB.displayText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.

CPDV.text: When you slumber, you shall not fear. When you rest, your sleep also will be sweet.
CPDV.displayText: When you slumber, you shall not fear. When you rest, your sleep also will be sweet.

verses.context: Part of a longer promise that wisdom brings safety, Solomon pictures a person lying down at night without fear and sleeping soundly.

KJV.text: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.
KJV.displayText: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

BSB.text: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.
BSB.displayText: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.

CPDV.text: The expectation of the just is rejoicing. But the hope of the impious will perish.
CPDV.displayText: The expectation of the just is rejoicing. But the hope of the impious will perish.

verses.context: Contrasting the outcomes awaiting the righteous and the wicked, Solomon promises hope brings gladness while wicked expectation comes to nothing.

KJV.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
KJV.displayText: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

BSB.text: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
BSB.displayText: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

CPDV.text: The soul that blesses shall be made fat. And whoever inebriates will likewise be inebriated himself.
CPDV.displayText: The soul that blesses shall be made fat. And whoever inebriates will likewise be inebriated himself.

verses.context: Praising generosity, Solomon observes that the person who gives freely ends up enriched, and the one who refreshes others is refreshed in turn.

KJV.text: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
KJV.displayText: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.

BSB.text: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
BSB.displayText: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

CPDV.text: He who makes promises is also jabbed, as if with a sword, in conscience. But the tongue of the wise is reasonable.
CPDV.displayText: He who makes promises is also jabbed, as if with a sword, in conscience. But the tongue of the wise is reasonable.

verses.context: Contrasting careless and wise speech, Solomon compares reckless words to a sword's cutting wound, while the wise person's words bring healing.

KJV.text: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
KJV.displayText: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

BSB.text: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
BSB.displayText: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

CPDV.text: The well-being of the heart is life for the flesh. But envy is decay for the bones.
CPDV.displayText: The well-being of the heart is life for the flesh. But envy is decay for the bones.

verses.context: Comparing inward states rather than outward circumstances, Solomon credits a peaceful heart with giving life to the body, while envy rots it from within.

KJV.text: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
KJV.displayText: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.

BSB.text: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
BSB.displayText: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.

CPDV.text: A rejoicing heart gladdens the face. But by the grief of the soul, the spirit is cast down.
CPDV.displayText: A rejoicing heart gladdens the face. But by the grief of the soul, the spirit is cast down.

verses.context: Turning to matters of the heart, Solomon observes that a cheerful heart shows on the face, while sorrow of heart breaks the spirit.

KJV.text: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy is he.
KJV.displayText: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy is he.

BSB.text: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
BSB.displayText: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.

CPDV.text: The learned in word shall find good things. And whoever hopes in the Lord is blessed.
CPDV.displayText: The learned in word shall find good things. And whoever hopes in the Lord is blessed.

verses.context: Linking practical skill to spiritual trust, Solomon promises good outcomes to whoever handles matters wisely and happiness to the one who trusts the Lord.

KJV.text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.
KJV.displayText: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

BSB.text: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
BSB.displayText: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.

CPDV.text: Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships. Whoever repeats the words of another separates allies.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever conceals an offense seeks friendships. Whoever repeats the words of another separates allies.

verses.context: On handling another's fault, Solomon praises the one who covers an offense out of love, over the one who gossips and divides close friends.

KJV.text: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
KJV.displayText: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

BSB.text: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
BSB.displayText: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.

CPDV.text: The doctrine of a man is known through patience. And his glory is to pass beyond iniquities.
CPDV.displayText: The doctrine of a man is known through patience. And his glory is to pass beyond iniquities.

verses.context: Praising self-control over quick offense, Solomon credits wisdom with delaying anger, treating overlooking an insult as honorable rather than weak.

KJV.text: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.
KJV.displayText: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.

BSB.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
BSB.displayText: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

CPDV.text: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the Lord, and he will free you.
CPDV.displayText: Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Wait for the Lord, and he will free you.

verses.context: Countering the urge toward personal revenge, Solomon instructs the wronged person to wait on the Lord for deliverance instead of repaying evil directly.

KJV.text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.
KJV.displayText: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.

BSB.text: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
BSB.displayText: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.

CPDV.text: The horse is prepared for the day of battle. But the Lord bestows salvation.
CPDV.displayText: The horse is prepared for the day of battle. But the Lord bestows salvation.

verses.context: Closing a chapter weighing human planning against God's sovereignty, Solomon notes a war-horse can be readied, but victory ultimately belongs to the Lord.

KJV.text: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
KJV.displayText: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.

BSB.text: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
BSB.displayText: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!

CPDV.text: If you despair, being weary in the day of anguish, your strength will be diminished.
CPDV.displayText: If you despair, being weary in the day of anguish, your strength will be diminished.

verses.context: Speaking plainly about crisis, Solomon observes that a person's true strength, or the lack of it, shows most clearly on a hard day.

KJV.text: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
KJV.displayText: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

BSB.text: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.
BSB.displayText: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.

CPDV.text: So, too, is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul. When you have found it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.
CPDV.displayText: So, too, is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul. When you have found it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.

verses.context: Comparing wisdom to honey a son is urged to taste, Solomon promises that finding it brings a real future reward rather than disappointment.

KJV.text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.
KJV.displayText: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.

BSB.text: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
BSB.displayText: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.

CPDV.text: Whoever fears man will quickly fall. Whoever hopes in the Lord shall be lifted up.
CPDV.displayText: Whoever fears man will quickly fall. Whoever hopes in the Lord shall be lifted up.

verses.context: Contrasting two sources of security, Solomon warns that fearing what people think becomes a trap, while trusting the Lord keeps a person safe.

KJV.text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
KJV.displayText: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

BSB.text: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
BSB.displayText: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.

CPDV.text: Who shall find a strong woman? Far away, and from the furthest parts, is her price.
CPDV.displayText: Who shall find a strong woman? Far away, and from the furthest parts, is her price.

verses.context: Opening the closing poem of Proverbs, this verse poses a question about the rare value of a capable, virtuous woman, worth more than costly jewels.

KJV.text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
KJV.displayText: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.

BSB.text: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
BSB.displayText: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!

CPDV.text: If one falls, he shall be supported by the other. Woe to one who is alone. For when he falls, he has no one to lift him up.
CPDV.displayText: If one falls, he shall be supported by the other. Woe to one who is alone. For when he falls, he has no one to lift him up.

verses.context: Reflecting on the value of companionship over isolation, the Preacher observes that a person who falls alone has no one there to help them up.

KJV.text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
KJV.displayText: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

BSB.text: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
BSB.displayText: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

CPDV.text: In the same manner that you do not know the way of the spirit, nor the way that bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the works of God, who is the Maker of all.
CPDV.displayText: In the same manner that you do not know the way of the spirit, nor the way that bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the works of God, who is the Maker of all.

verses.context: Comparing the mystery of the wind and of a child forming in the womb, the Preacher argues that God's ways are simply beyond full human understanding.

KJV.text: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
KJV.displayText: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

BSB.text: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
BSB.displayText: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

CPDV.text: Chorus to Groom and Bride: Capture for us the little foxes, which are tearing down the vines; for our vineyard has flourished. Bride to Chorus: My beloved is for me, and I am for him. He pastures among the lilies, until the day rises and the shadows decline. Bride to Groom: Return, O my beloved. Be like a doe and like a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.
CPDV.displayText: Chorus to Groom and Bride: Capture for us the little foxes, which are tearing down the vines; for our vineyard has flourished. Bride to Chorus: My beloved is for me, and I am for him. He pastures among the lilies, until the day rises and the shadows decline. Bride to Groom: Return, O my beloved. Be like a doe and like a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.

verses.context: In this love poem, the young woman describes her beloved as belonging entirely to her, picturing him among the lilies of the field.

KJV.text: And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.
KJV.displayText: And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.

BSB.text: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
BSB.displayText: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the LORD for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”

CPDV.text: And they will say in that day: “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us. This is the Lord! We have endured for him. We will exult and rejoice in his salvation.”
CPDV.displayText: And they will say in that day: “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us. This is the Lord! We have endured for him. We will exult and rejoice in his salvation.”

verses.context: Looking ahead to a day when death itself is swallowed up, Isaiah pictures God's people finally saying that the Lord they waited for has brought salvation.

KJV.text: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.
KJV.displayText: For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.

BSB.text: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.
BSB.displayText: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.

CPDV.text: For I am the Lord your God. I take you by your hand, and I say to you: Do not be afraid. I have helped you.
CPDV.displayText: For I am the Lord your God. I take you by your hand, and I say to you: Do not be afraid. I have helped you.

verses.context: Reassuring an anxious Israel, God through Isaiah promises to hold their right hand personally and tells them plainly not to be afraid.

KJV.text: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
KJV.displayText: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.

BSB.text: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.
BSB.displayText: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.

CPDV.text: Even to your old age, I am the same. And even with your grey hairs, I will carry you. I have made you, and I will sustain you. I will carry you, and I will save you.
CPDV.displayText: Even to your old age, I am the same. And even with your grey hairs, I will carry you. I have made you, and I will sustain you. I will carry you, and I will save you.

verses.context: Contrasting himself with idols that must be carried by their worshippers, God tells Israel through Isaiah that he is the one who carries his people, even into old age.

KJV.text: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
KJV.displayText: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.

BSB.text: For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite.
BSB.displayText: For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite.

CPDV.text: For this is said by the Most High, the Sublime One, who dwells in eternity. And his name is Holy, for he dwells in the exalted and holy place, and he acts with a restrained and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
CPDV.displayText: For this is said by the Most High, the Sublime One, who dwells in eternity. And his name is Holy, for he dwells in the exalted and holy place, and he acts with a restrained and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

verses.context: Describing God as both transcendent and near, Isaiah says the eternal, holy God chooses to dwell with those who are humble and repentant in heart.

KJV.text: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
KJV.displayText: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.

BSB.text: The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
BSB.displayText: The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.

CPDV.text: And the Lord will give you rest continually, and he will fill your soul with splendor, and he will free your bones, and you will be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters will not fail.
CPDV.displayText: And the Lord will give you rest continually, and he will fill your soul with splendor, and he will free your bones, and you will be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters will not fail.

verses.context: Explaining what true fasting looks like, Isaiah promises that caring for the hungry and afflicted will bring the Lord's continual guidance and refreshment.

KJV.text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
KJV.displayText: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.

BSB.text: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.
BSB.displayText: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.

CPDV.text: For behold, I create the new heavens and the new earth. And the former things will not be in memory and will not enter into the heart.
CPDV.displayText: For behold, I create the new heavens and the new earth. And the former things will not be in memory and will not enter into the heart.

verses.context: Looking far beyond present judgment, God announces through Isaiah a coming new creation so complete that the old troubles will not even be remembered.

KJV.text: Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.
KJV.displayText: Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.

BSB.text: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
BSB.displayText: Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.

CPDV.text: I discovered your words and I consumed them. And your word became to me as the gladness and joy of my heart. For your name has been invoked over me, O Lord, the God of hosts.
CPDV.displayText: I discovered your words and I consumed them. And your word became to me as the gladness and joy of my heart. For your name has been invoked over me, O Lord, the God of hosts.

verses.context: Despite his hard calling, Jeremiah tells God that receiving God's words brought him real joy, since he was known as one who carried God's name.

KJV.text: But the Lord is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten.
KJV.displayText: But the Lord is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten.

BSB.text: But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior. Therefore, my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. Since they have not succeeded, they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
BSB.displayText: But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior. Therefore, my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. Since they have not succeeded, they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.

CPDV.text: But the Lord is with me, like a strong warrior. For this reason, those who persecute me will fall, and they will be ineffective. They will be greatly confounded. For they have not understood the everlasting disgrace that will never be wiped away.
CPDV.displayText: But the Lord is with me, like a strong warrior. For this reason, those who persecute me will fall, and they will be ineffective. They will be greatly confounded. For they have not understood the everlasting disgrace that will never be wiped away.

verses.context: Even while lamenting the mockery and plots against him, Jeremiah declares confidence that the Lord stands with him like a fearsome warrior, so his enemies will fail.

KJV.text: Ah Lord God! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
KJV.displayText: Ah Lord God! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:

BSB.text: “Oh, Lord GOD! You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for You!
BSB.displayText: “Oh, Lord GOD! You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for You!

CPDV.text: Alas, alas, alas, O Lord God! Behold, you have made heaven and earth, by your great strength and by your outstretched arm. No word is difficult for you.
CPDV.displayText: Alas, alas, alas, O Lord God! Behold, you have made heaven and earth, by your great strength and by your outstretched arm. No word is difficult for you.

verses.context: After buying a field as a sign of future hope even while Jerusalem is besieged, Jeremiah prays, marveling that nothing is too difficult for the God who made heaven and earth.

KJV.text: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
KJV.displayText: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

BSB.text: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.
BSB.displayText: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.

CPDV.text: For behold our God, whom we worship, is able to rescue us from the oven of burning fire and to free us from your hands, O king.

verses.context: Immediately after affirming God's power to save them, the three men add that even if he chooses not to, they will still refuse to worship the king's image.

verses.context: Picturing God as a parent teaching a child to walk, Hosea describes God drawing wayward Israel gently, with cords of love rather than force.

verses.context: Closing his prophecy with praise rather than accusation, Micah marvels that God is unlike any other in his willingness to forgive and delight in mercy.

verses.context: While Saul hunts him in the wilderness of Ziph, David is found and encouraged by Jonathan, who comes to strengthen his friend's resolve in God.

KJV.text: Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.
KJV.displayText: Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.

BSB.displayText: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”

CPDV.text: Blessed is the Lord your God, whom you have greatly pleased, and who has placed you upon the throne of Israel. For the Lord loves Israel forever, and he has appointed you as king, so that you may accomplish judgment and justice.”
CPDV.displayText: Blessed is the Lord your God, whom you have greatly pleased, and who has placed you upon the throne of Israel. For the Lord loves Israel forever, and he has appointed you as king, so that you may accomplish judgment and justice.”

verses.context: Having traveled to test Solomon's famed wisdom and seen it exceed the reports, the queen of Sheba blesses the Lord for placing him on Israel's throne.

KJV.text: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
KJV.displayText: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

BSB.text: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
BSB.displayText: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.

CPDV.text: He accomplishes great and incomprehensible and miraculous things, which cannot be numbered.
CPDV.displayText: He accomplishes great and incomprehensible and miraculous things, which cannot be numbered.

verses.context: Answering his friends, Job pauses to acknowledge God's incomprehensible power, doing wonders and great works beyond human understanding.

KJV.text: But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.
KJV.displayText: But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.

BSB.text: But I have trusted in Your loving devotion; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
BSB.displayText: But I have trusted in Your loving devotion; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.

CPDV.text: But I have hoped in your mercy. My heart will exult in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who assigns good things to me. And I will sing psalms to the name of the Lord Most High.
CPDV.displayText: But I have hoped in your mercy. My heart will exult in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who assigns good things to me. And I will sing psalms to the name of the Lord Most High.

verses.context: After repeatedly asking God how long his suffering will last, David pivots in the same psalm to declare his trust in God's unfailing love.

KJV.text: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
KJV.displayText: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

BSB.text: I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
BSB.displayText: I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.

CPDV.text: I have made provision for the Lord always in my sight. For he is at my right hand, so that I may not be disturbed.
CPDV.displayText: I have made provision for the Lord always in my sight. For he is at my right hand, so that I may not be disturbed.

verses.context: Reflecting on God's constant presence, David describes keeping the Lord set before him so steadily that nothing can shake him.

KJV.text: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the Lord.
KJV.displayText: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the Lord.

BSB.text: Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.
BSB.displayText: Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.

CPDV.text: Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord.

verses.context: Closing a psalm that moves from crisis to confidence, David encourages all who hope in the Lord to take courage and let God strengthen their hearts.

KJV.text: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.
KJV.displayText: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

BSB.text: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
BSB.displayText: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.

CPDV.text: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and confirm me with an unsurpassed spirit.
CPDV.displayText: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and confirm me with an unsurpassed spirit.

verses.context: In this psalm of repentance written after his sin with Bathsheba, David asks God not merely to forgive him but to restore the joy he has lost.

KJV.text: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
KJV.displayText: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

BSB.text: A Psalm of David, when he was in the Wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water.
BSB.displayText: O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water.

CPDV.text: O God, my God: to you, I keep vigil until first light. For you, my soul has thirsted, to you my body, in so many ways.
CPDV.displayText: O God, my God: to you, I keep vigil until first light. For you, my soul has thirsted, to you my body, in so many ways.

verses.context: Composed while David was in the wilderness of Judah, this psalm opens by comparing his longing for God to a thirst in a dry and waterless land.

KJV.text: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord God, that I may declare all thy works.
KJV.displayText: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord God, that I may declare all thy works.

BSB.text: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.
BSB.displayText: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.

CPDV.text: But it is good for me to adhere to God, to put my hope in the Lord God, so that I may announce all your prophecies, at the gates of the daughter of Zion.
CPDV.displayText: But it is good for me to adhere to God, to put my hope in the Lord God, so that I may announce all your prophecies, at the gates of the daughter of Zion.

verses.context: Concluding his struggle over why evil people seem to prosper, Asaph decides that drawing near to God is simply better than anything else.

KJV.text: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
KJV.displayText: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.

BSB.text: But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.
BSB.displayText: But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.

CPDV.text: And you, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful, being patient and full of mercy and truthful.
CPDV.displayText: And you, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful, being patient and full of mercy and truthful.

verses.context: Appealing for mercy against violent enemies, David grounds his hope in a description of God's character as compassionate, gracious, and full of mercy and truth.

KJV.text: I wait for the Lord, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.
KJV.displayText: I wait for the Lord, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.

BSB.text: I wait for the LORD; my soul does wait, and in His word I put my hope.
BSB.displayText: I wait for the LORD; my soul does wait, and in His word I put my hope.

CPDV.text: My soul has hoped in the Lord.
CPDV.displayText: My soul has hoped in the Lord.

verses.context: Crying up from a place of deep distress, the psalmist describes waiting for the Lord the way someone might wait through a long night, hoping in his word.

KJV.text: The Lord is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.
KJV.displayText: The Lord is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

BSB.text: The LORD is good to all; His compassion rests on all He has made.
BSB.displayText: The LORD is good to all; His compassion rests on all He has made.

CPDV.text: The Lord is sweet to all things, and his compassion is upon all his works.
CPDV.displayText: The Lord is sweet to all things, and his compassion is upon all his works.

verses.context: In this alphabetic psalm of praise, David widens his focus from Israel alone to declare that the Lord's goodness and mercy extend over everything he made.

KJV.text: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.
KJV.displayText: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.

BSB.text: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.
BSB.displayText: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit.

CPDV.text: Great is our Lord, and great is his virtue. And of his wisdom, there is no number.
CPDV.displayText: Great is our Lord, and great is his virtue. And of his wisdom, there is no number.

verses.context: Praising God for both cosmic power and personal care, such as knowing every star by name, this psalm marvels that his understanding has no limit.

KJV.text: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.
KJV.displayText: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.

BSB.text: For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
BSB.displayText: For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.

CPDV.text: For the Lord bestows wisdom, and out of his mouth, prudence and knowledge.
CPDV.displayText: For the Lord bestows wisdom, and out of his mouth, prudence and knowledge.

verses.context: Addressing a son seeking wisdom, Solomon names the Lord himself as the actual source from which wisdom and knowledge come.

KJV.text: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:
KJV.displayText: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:

BSB.text: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
BSB.displayText: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.

CPDV.text: Let not mercy and truth abandon you: encircle them around your throat, and inscribe them on the tablets of your heart.
CPDV.displayText: Let not mercy and truth abandon you: encircle them around your throat, and inscribe them on the tablets of your heart.

verses.context: Instructing a son in wise living, Solomon urges him to hold onto mercy and truth so closely they become like something written on his own heart.

KJV.text: But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
KJV.displayText: But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

BSB.text: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
BSB.displayText: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.

CPDV.text: But the path of the just is like a shining light: it advances and increases, even to the day of completion.
CPDV.displayText: But the path of the just is like a shining light: it advances and increases, even to the day of completion.

verses.context: Contrasting two ways of living, Solomon describes the righteous person's path as a light that keeps growing brighter until full daylight.

KJV.text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.
KJV.displayText: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

BSB.text: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.
BSB.displayText: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.

CPDV.text: I love those who love me. And those who stand watch for me until morning shall discover me.
CPDV.displayText: I love those who love me. And those who stand watch for me until morning shall discover me.

verses.context: Speaking here in the voice of personified Wisdom herself, this saying promises that those who love and diligently seek her will find her.

KJV.text: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.
KJV.displayText: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.

BSB.text: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.
BSB.displayText: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.

CPDV.text: The blessing of the Lord causes riches. Affliction will not be a companion to them.
CPDV.displayText: The blessing of the Lord causes riches. Affliction will not be a companion to them.

verses.context: Among Solomon's contrasts between the righteous and the wicked, he credits the Lord's blessing with bringing wealth that carries no accompanying grief.

KJV.text: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
KJV.displayText: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.

BSB.text: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
BSB.displayText: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.

CPDV.text: In the fear of the Lord is the faithfulness of strength, and there shall be hope for his sons.
CPDV.displayText: In the fear of the Lord is the faithfulness of strength, and there shall be hope for his sons.

verses.context: Among sayings on wisdom and family, Solomon links reverence for the Lord to a strong sense of security that extends even to one's children.

KJV.text: All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast.
KJV.displayText: All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast.

BSB.text: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
BSB.displayText: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

CPDV.text: All the days of the poor are evil. A secure mind is like a continual feast.
CPDV.displayText: All the days of the poor are evil. A secure mind is like a continual feast.

verses.context: Continuing on inner disposition, Solomon contrasts the afflicted person's constant hardship with the merry heart's ongoing feast.

KJV.text: By humility and the fear of the Lord are riches, and honour, and life.
KJV.displayText: By humility and the fear of the Lord are riches, and honour, and life.

BSB.text: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
BSB.displayText: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.

CPDV.displayText: The end of moderation is the fear of the Lord, riches and glory and life.

verses.context: Pairing two qualities together, Solomon credits humility joined with reverence for the Lord as the source of riches, honor, and a full life.

KJV.text: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
KJV.displayText: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.

BSB.text: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
BSB.displayText: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.

CPDV.text: For you will have hope in the end, and your expectation will not be taken away.
CPDV.displayText: For you will have hope in the end, and your expectation will not be taken away.

verses.context: Advising against envying the apparent success of sinners, the father in this instruction assures his son there is a future ahead and hope will not be cut off.

KJV.text: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.
KJV.displayText: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.

BSB.text: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
BSB.displayText: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.

CPDV.displayText: Every word of God is fire-tested. He is a bronze shield to those who hope in him.

verses.context: In sayings attributed to a lesser-known figure named Agur, this line affirms that every word from God is trustworthy, a shield for those who rely on him.

KJV.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
KJV.displayText: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

BSB.text: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.
BSB.displayText: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.

CPDV.text: In good times, enjoy good things, but beware of an evil time. For just as God has established the one, so also the other, in order that man may not find any just complaint against him.
CPDV.displayText: In good times, enjoy good things, but beware of an evil time. For just as God has established the one, so also the other, in order that man may not find any just complaint against him.

verses.context: Weighing good days against bad ones, the Preacher advises enjoying prosperity while it lasts and reflecting during adversity, since God allows both to come.

KJV.text: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;
KJV.displayText: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;

BSB.text: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
BSB.displayText: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.

CPDV.displayText: And my people will be seated in the beauty of peacefulness, and in the tabernacles of faithfulness, and in the opulence of restfulness.

verses.context: Looking past coming judgment to eventual restoration, Isaiah promises that God's people will finally dwell in peaceful, secure homes.

KJV.text: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.
KJV.displayText: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.

BSB.displayText: Say to those with anxious hearts: “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.”

CPDV.text: Say to the fainthearted: “Take courage and fear not! Behold, your God will bring the vindication of retribution. God himself will arrive to save you.”
CPDV.displayText: Say to the fainthearted: “Take courage and fear not! Behold, your God will bring the vindication of retribution. God himself will arrive to save you.”

verses.context: Speaking to those weakened by fear, Isaiah urges courage, promising that God himself is coming to bring vengeance on their behalf and save them.

KJV.text: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the Lord will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them.
KJV.displayText: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the Lord will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them.

BSB.displayText: The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

CPDV.text: The indigent and the poor are seeking water, but there is none. Their tongue has been dried up by thirst. I, the Lord, will heed them. I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
CPDV.displayText: The indigent and the poor are seeking water, but there is none. Their tongue has been dried up by thirst. I, the Lord, will heed them. I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.

verses.context: Picturing the desperate thirst of the poor, Isaiah has God promise that when they cry out for water, he himself, Israel's God, will answer and not abandon them.

KJV.text: Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.
KJV.displayText: Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.

BSB.displayText: Thus says the LORD your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your benefit, who directs you in the way you should go.

CPDV.text: Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord, your God, who teaches you beneficial things, who guides you in the way that you walk.
CPDV.displayText: Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord, your God, who teaches you beneficial things, who guides you in the way that you walk.

verses.context: Identifying himself as Israel's Redeemer, God speaks through Isaiah as the teacher who instructs his people and leads them in the way they should go.

KJV.text: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.
KJV.displayText: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee.

BSB.displayText: Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

CPDV.displayText: For the mountains will be moved, and the hills will tremble. But my mercy will not depart from you, and the covenant of my peace will not be shaken, said the Lord, who has compassion on you.

verses.context: Comparing God's covenant faithfulness to something more permanent than mountains, Isaiah promises that God's kindness toward his people will never depart.

KJV.text: Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near:
KJV.displayText: Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near:

BSB.displayText: Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near.

CPDV.displayText: Seek the Lord, while he is able to be found. Call upon him, while he is near.

verses.context: Urging a response to God's offer of mercy, Isaiah calls people to seek the Lord while he can still be found and to call on him while he is near.

KJV.displayText: Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.

BSB.displayText: Your sun will no longer set, and your moon will not wane; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your sorrow will cease.

CPDV.displayText: Your sun will no longer set, and your moon will not diminish. For the Lord will be an everlasting light for you, and the days of your mourning will be completed.

verses.context: Picturing Jerusalem's future glory, Isaiah promises a light that never sets and an end to the mourning that once marked her days.

BSB.displayText: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to the prisoners,

CPDV.displayText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, for the Lord has anointed me. He has sent me to bring good news to the meek, so as to heal the contrite of heart, to preach leniency to captives and release to the confined,

verses.context: Speaking in the voice of an anointed messenger, Isaiah describes a mission to bring good news to the poor and freedom to captives, later read aloud by Jesus in Luke's Gospel.

KJV.text: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.
KJV.displayText: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.
